key_insight: Preferred particle orientations increase average sunlight exposure by 5–40% relative to random orientations in wind-driven surface flows.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for particle shape and orientation can improve sunlight-exposure estimates for microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice near the water surface.
method: Measure particle depth and orientation in a laboratory wind-wave tank.
Use measurements to model sunlight exposure in an aquatic environment.
Compare disk and rod irradiance as particle mixing length relative to light decay length changes.
evidence_signal: All tested cases showed preferred orientations, while disks exhibited disproportionately greater mean irradiance at smaller mixing-length-to-light-decay-length ratios.
watch_item: The reported exposure increases come from a model informed by laboratory measurements; applicability to natural waters requires validation.
paper_title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
